findings.issue_text: isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && instead of || between isTeamAdmin(...) and isTeamOwner(...), so the condition is effectively always false since a user can't be both admin and owner simultaneously, blocking team admins/owners from adding guests

Backend addGuests schema lacks a uniqueness constraint on the guests array (unlike the client-side schema refine), and the handler only dedupes against existing booking attendees, not within the submitted array itself, allowing duplicate attendee rows via direct API calls with duplicate emails

eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees call is not wrapped in try/catch, so if it throws after prisma.booking.update already persisted new attendees, the mutation fails for the client while DB and calendar end up inconsistent with no rollback
Blacklist filtering lowercases blacklistedGuestEmails but compares against raw-cased guest values, allowing a blacklisted email with different casing to bypass the block
sendAddGuestsEmails is called with the raw unfiltered guests input instead of uniqueGuests, causing already-existing attendees to be misclassified as new and receive the wrong email template

In AddGuestsDialog.tsx, the error message template literal is always a non-empty string, so the || t("unable_to_add_guests") fallback never triggers even when err.data/err.message are undefined, producing a message like "undefined: undefined"
The catch block for sendAddGuestsEmails discards the actual error and uses console.log instead of a proper logger/console.error, making email delivery failures unobservable

goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees call is not wrapped in try/catch, so if it throws after prisma.booking.update already persisted new attendees, the mutation fails for the client while DB and calendar end up inconsistent with no rollback

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the code persists new attendees via prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...) before calling eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking). That updateCalendarAttendees call is not inside a try/catch (only sendAddGuestsEmails is), and there is no DB transaction/rollback around the sequence. If updateCalendarAttendees throws (plausible since it likely performs external calendar updates), the mutation will error after the DB has already been updated, leaving DB attendees changed while the external calendar may not be updated—an inconsistency introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: sendAddGuestsEmails is called with the raw unfiltered guests input instead of uniqueGuests, causing already-existing attendees to be misclassified as new and receive the wrong email template

adjudication.rationale:
In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler computes `uniqueGuests` by filtering out emails that already exist in `booking.attendees` (and blacklisted). It then only `createMany` for `uniqueGuests`, so only those are actually new attendees.

However, the email dispatch uses the raw `guests` input: `await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests);` instead of `uniqueGuests`. In `sendAddGuestsEmails` (in `email-manager.ts`), attendee emails are classified by `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email)) { ...AttendeeScheduledEmail... } else { ...AttendeeAddGuestsEmail... }`. Because `evt.attendees` includes existing attendees, if the caller included an already-existing attendee email in the input, that attendee will match `newGuests.includes(...)` and be treated as “new”, receiving `AttendeeScheduledEmail` instead of the “guests added” template.

This is a concrete, verifiable mismatch introduced by passing `guests` rather than `uniqueGuests`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In AddGuestsDialog.tsx, the error message template literal is always a non-empty string, so the || t("unable_to_add_guests") fallback never triggers even when err.data/err.message are undefined, producing a message like "undefined: undefined"

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` the `onError` handler does `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` and then `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")`. A template literal always produces a string, so `message` will be truthy even if `err.data?.code` and/or `err.message` are `undefined`, resulting in a toast like `"undefined: undefined"` (or similar) and the fallback will never run. This is a real correctness issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The catch block for sendAddGuestsEmails discards the actual error and uses console.log instead of a proper logger/console.error, making email delivery failures unobservable

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, the `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` block catches any failure but does not log/record `err` (no message/stack) and uses `console.log` with a generic string. This discards the actual error details, significantly reducing observability/debuggability of email delivery failures introduced by this new feature.
